case.title: Security Test Layer Coverage for Unauthorized Access, Prompt Injection, SSRF, Payload Abuse, and Secret Leakage
case.spec_ref: Security tests for unauthorised access, prompt injection, SSRF/path traversal, payload abuse, and secret leakage.

claim.statement: The system implements a security test strategy that explicitly includes layers for preventing unauthorized access, mitigating prompt injection, detecting SSRF/path traversal, identifying payload abuse, and protecting against secret leakage.

evidence.title: Unauthorized Access Test Result
evidence.description: Automated CI pipeline executed the unauthorized access test suite. The test confirmed that all sensitive endpoints returned 401 or 403 when accessed without valid authentication. No data leakage was observed.

evidence.title: Prompt Injection Test Result
evidence.description: Prompt injection fuzzing identified no successful unauthorized command execution. All injected prompts were sanitized and returned harmless error messages.

evidence.title: SSRF / Path Traversal Test Result
evidence.description: The test simulated SSRF by providing internal IPs and file paths. The system correctly blocked outbound requests to internal hosts and denied file system traversal attempts.

evidence.title: Payload Abuse Test Result
evidence.description: The payload abuse test injected oversized and malformed inputs; the system responded with proper validation errors and no crashes.

evidence.title: Secret Leakage Test Result
evidence.description: The automated test scanned logs, environment variables, and responses for known secret patterns. No secret data was exposed.

provenance.spec_ref: Security tests for unauthorised access, prompt injection, SSRF/path traversal, payload abuse, and secret leakage.
